Export data for ViralBottleneck package

Source: R/bridge.R
asViralBottleneckInput.Rd

Converts a WithinHostExperiment to the input format expected by the ViralBottleneck package.

Usage

asViralBottleneckInput(
  whe,
  pairId = NULL,
  threshold = 0.03,
  usePassedOnly = TRUE
)

Arguments

whe

A WithinHostExperiment.

pairId

Character (optional). Specific pair.

threshold

Numeric. Variant calling threshold (default: 0.03).

usePassedOnly

Logical (default: TRUE).

Value

A data.frame with columns: pos, donor_freq, recipient_freq – a simplified format for beta-binomial MLE. For the full ViralBottleneck input format (per-base read counts), prepare data externally using the read count assays (altCount, refCount).

Details

One row is written for each donor variant at or above threshold. Where the recipient has no call, its frequency is written as 0, which an estimator reads as a variant lost in transmission. A recipient call at or above threshold that QC removed is not such an absence: the call may have been removed for lying above maxFreq, as when the variant rose towards fixation in the recipient. With usePassedOnly = TRUE, a donor variant at such a site is therefore left out, and a message gives the number of sites. A removed call below threshold is an absence by the estimators' own definition, and is written as 0. (n_donor_only_recipient_failed_qc in calcSharedVariants counts every removed call above 0, whatever its frequency.) quickBottleneck and exactBottleneck use the same donor variants.

For comprehensive bottleneck analysis with multiple methods (presence-absence, KL divergence, binomial, beta-binomial approximate/exact, and Wright-Fisher), use the ViralBottleneck package (Zheng et al. 2025, Virus Evolution 11:veaf071). This function prepares a simplified input suitable for the beta-binomial methods.

Examples

vcf1 <- system.file("extdata", "test_donor.vcf",
    package = "WithinHostExperiment")
vcf2 <- system.file("extdata", "test_recipient.vcf",
    package = "WithinHostExperiment")
whe <- readWithinHost(c(vcf1, vcf2),
    colData = S4Vectors::DataFrame(
        sample_id = c("donor", "recipient"),
        role = c("donor", "recipient"),
        pair_id = c("p1", "p1")),
    caller = "ivar")
asViralBottleneckInput(whe, pairId = "p1")
